requirements.evidence: All schema requirements are present: `entities` has the named `entities_slug_unique` index and soft deletes (database/migrations/2026_10_29_000000_create_entities_table.php:14-20), and `entity_memberships` has cascade FKs, `role` default employee, the `(entity_id, user_id)` unique, and the portable `owner_seq` generated column plus `entity_memberships_one_owner` (database/migrations/2026_10_29_000001_create_entity_memberships_table.php:18-29). Policy rules match the task (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:10-35; app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:10-59); `pick` authorizes before writing the session and audits (app/Http/Controllers/EntityController.php:12-24); the three pages authorize in mount and re-authorize every action (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:27-96; app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:27-105); edge cases (last manager, owner row, foreign membership id, owner-only settings URL, soft-deleted slug) are handled and covered.

conventions.evidence: Most conventions are followed: generated-style reversible migrations, `#[Fillable]` (app/Models/Entity.php:14; app/Models/EntityMembership.php:13), policy-based authorization, an extracted `x-entity-nav` Blade component (resources/views/components/entity-nav.blade.php:1-14), and docs/CHANGELOG updates. However, every domain write is done inside the Livewire components rather than in `app/Actions/*` (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:49,96; app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:51,69-72,102-106), and Livewire validation is inline `$this->validate([...])`/`validator()` rather than the project's `#[Validate]`/`rules()` pattern (Members.php:23,39-41,70-72; Settings.php:21-25,40-47).

security.evidence: Every public action authorizes server-side on the model resolved through the locked entity (`Members.php:37,68,92`; `Settings.php:38,66-67,88`), `$entity` is `#[Locked]` (Members.php:20-21; Settings.php:18-19), action parameters are resolved through `$this->entity->memberships()` (Members.php:129-132), and Blade escapes all output. `pick` authorizes before touching the session (EntityController.php:15-17). The one gap: `verified` is only route middleware (routes/web.php:53); Livewire does not persist it on `/livewire/update` requests and no `Livewire::addPersistentMiddleware` call exists, so the verified check covers only the first page load. Actions remain policy-authorized, so impact is limited.

tests.evidence: Broad Pest coverage: schema/index/owner_seq and cascade behaviour (tests/Feature/EntityDataModelTest.php:14-118), the full policy matrix (EntityPoliciesTest.php:20-110), pick/session/guest/unverified/stale-session (EntityPickTest.php:12-64), page 403s and link hiding (EntityPagesTest.php:21-98), member add/assign/remove with owner, last-manager, foreign-id and locked-entity cases (EntityMembersTest.php:26-176), and settings save/delete/transfer with tamper and validation cases (EntitySettingsTest.php:24-188). Gaps: the last EntityPickTest test never calls `pick` (EntityPickTest.php:66-68); the 'defaults to employee' test always supplies `role` through the factory (EntityDataModelTest.php:76-81); and the owner-vanished transfer test fails at mount authorization before `transfer()`'s own null check (EntitySettingsTest.php:165-171).

simplicity.evidence: Lean overall: reuses `x-form-field`/`x-button`, extracts `x-entity-nav`, keeps one membership lookup helper (Members.php:126-132), and adds no service/repository layer. Minor duplication remains between `EntityPolicy::hasRole` (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:39-44) and `EntityMembershipPolicy::isManager` (app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:42-47), and `Settings::delete` checks both `manageSettings` and `delete` (Settings.php:66-67).

readability.evidence: Small, focused methods with clear names (`addMember`/`assignRole`/`removeMember`, `save`/`delete`/`transfer`), helpful comments on non-obvious decisions (Members.php:44-45; Settings.php:69-71,104), consistent formatting with sibling files, and no debug output or dead code visible. The only slightly harder-to-follow part is the split lookup/transaction in `Settings::transfer` (Settings.php:90-106), which is called out separately.

scope.evidence: Every added or changed file serves the task: models, enum, policies, factories, migrations (app/Models/Entity.php, EntityMembership.php, UserRole.php; app/Policies/*; database/*), the pick controller, the three Livewire components and Blade views, routes, both lang files, tests, docs/database-schema.md and CHANGELOG.md. No unrelated refactor or out-of-scope feature; the extra audit lines/flash messages are small and on-topic.

issues.explanation: All domain writes (membership create/update/delete, entity update/delete, ownership transfer) are executed directly in Livewire components; the project requires one `app/Actions/*` class per use case with authorization inside the action.

Livewire input properties are validated with inline rules (`$this->validate([...])` / `validator()`) instead of the project's `#[Validate]` attributes or a `rules()` method; the public `$status` property is also client-writable rather than locked.

The `verified` middleware is not registered as persistent Livewire middleware, so `/livewire/update` requests do not enforce it; only the initial page load is verified. Policy authorization still guards every action, so impact is limited.

`transfer()` runs `lockForUpdate()` and the owner/target/403 checks outside `DB::transaction()`, so the locks are released immediately and a concurrent owner deletion or transfer can make the checks stale; move the reads and checks inside the transaction so the required 403 is reliable.
The document now says `entities` is implemented but still lists `locale_default`, a column the migration does not create, so the implemented schema and the doc disagree.

The last pick test never calls `pick`, the 'defaults to employee' test always supplies `role` through the factory, and the owner-vanished transfer test stops at mount authorization before `transfer()`'s own null check, so these cases are only nominally covered.
Both policies reimplement the same membership/role lookup; extracting it (for example on `User` or into one private helper) would remove the duplication.

review.summary: The change implements the entities and memberships feature end to end: schema with the portable one-owner constraint, policies, entity picking, and the dashboard, members and settings Livewire pages, backed by a broad Pest suite and solid server-side authorization. It is functionally complete, but it performs every domain write directly in the Livewire components instead of the required `app/Actions/*` layer, uses inline validation instead of the project's `#[Validate]` pattern, and moves the transfer lookups/locking outside the transaction. Those issues should be fixed before merging.
